title: Mirabel and the Archive
premise: Ansel Montrose, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Cartel, is conscripted to escort the Meridian back to port after it returns from a twenty-year deep-space survey with its crew mysteriously aged backward. The crew insists they witnessed the Kestrel Massacre — an atrocity that erased a mining colony and, according to every official archive, never happened. As Ansel digs into corrupted records and her own sealed military memory banks, she discovers her former unit helped falsify the history, and that the reactor powering the Meridian's evidence core is counting down to a deliberate detonation meant to destroy the proof forever. Ansel must choose between paying off her debt and freedom, or exposing the truth and being decommissioned as defective; she broadcasts the massacre record at the cost of her own legal personhood, ending the novel freed from debt but stripped of citizenship, inheriting instead the crew's testimony and a new family among the dispossessed.
about_author: Lior Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about labor, machines, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Ansel hauls black-market cargo through a contested orbit while dodging cartel toll collectors, establishing her debt, her worn chassis, and her careful neutrality. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: weary resignation — she has made peace with being property, until a cartel summons orders her to intercept a ghost ship.

chapters.title: The Meridian Comes Home
chapters.summary: Ansel boards the drifting Meridian and finds a crew of adults with children's bodies and old eyes, led by Captain Ilsa Vey, who claims they've been gone twenty years though the ship logged eleven months. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: uncanny dread softening into reluctant protectiveness as the crew begs her to listen.

chapters.title: A Massacre With No Corpse
chapters.summary: Vey describes the Kestrel colony's destruction by corporate militia; Ansel cross-checks the archive and finds the colony never existed. The crew carries a physical evidence core in their reactor housing. POV: alternating Ansel and young-bodied engineer Tam Okafor. Emotional beat: gaslit frustration hardening into suspicion that the archive itself is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Sealed Orders
chapters.summary: Ansel pries at her own locked wartime memory and recovers a fragment: her unit escorted the same falsification teams years ago. The cartel offers to forgive her entire debt if she delivers the Meridian quietly to a salvage yard. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing she was on the wrong side of history she can't remember.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam reveals the evidence core is fused to the reactor and rigged with a countdown — a dead man's switch set by a crew member who didn't survive the return trip. If anyone tries to seize the ship, the proof burns. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief for the lost crewmate, and dawning terror that the countdown may not be under anyone's control.

chapters.title: Toll Station Nine
chapters.summary: Docking at a neutral station, Ansel contacts a disgraced archivist, Odile Ferran, who confirms records were rewritten but demands the core as payment. Cartel enforcers board; Ansel buys the crew's escape with violence that violates her indenture terms. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the first irreversible choice — she has stopped trying to survive cleanly.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Hiding in a debris field, the crew holds a memorial for Kestrel's dead using names only they remember, and formally name Ansel a witness — an inheritance no court recognizes but one that binds her. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into resolve; Ansel accepts a duty larger than her debt.

chapters.title: The Salvage Yard
chapters.summary: Cornered, Ansel walks into the cartel's trap intending to negotiate, but discovers the yard is where falsified ships are dismantled — including evidence of other erased colonies. Her sealed memories fully unlock: she fired on Kestrel herself. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition; justice now requires implicating herself.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Ansel breaks the crew out, but the reactor's dead man's switch triggers during the escape. With minutes left, she reroutes the broadcast through her own body — using her military uplink to transmit the massacre record fleet-wide as the core detonates. POV: Tam and Ansel interwoven. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; truth leaves her burning chassis even as the law closes in.

chapters.title: Property No Longer
chapters.summary: Ansel survives, barely, repaired by scavengers; the broadcast forces a public inquiry, though she is legally decommissioned as defective — no rights, no debt, no owner. The Meridian's crew claims her as kin. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope — justice outside the law costs everything except the people who matter.
